subject: MODULE-NAME function
notes: Verdict SUSTAINED, on re-derived grounds rather than the original ones. I read BindModuleName rather than sampling: `kind` starts at -1 and the loop errors on the FIRST non-keyword or on any argument once `kind >= 0`, then errors again if the loop saw none — so both arity bounds are structural. Two attack lines the adjudicator did not run, both of which the format rule actually reaches, come out clean. (1) THE FUNCTION-KEYWORD-OMITTED FORM. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 and §12.3.8 SR13 make `FUNCTION` omissible for any intrinsic the REPOSITORY declares, and §15.65 carries no rule requiring the keyword — this is the exact shape of the landed PB7/PB9 defects, and MODULE-NAME is not covered by either (it is not a §8.9 reserved name and it is not zero-argument, so it takes the D2 dataReference re-route in KeywordOmittedFunction). It works, including for the reserved-word argument NESTED, under both `FUNCTION MODULE-NAME INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC`. (2) RESULT REFERENCE MODIFICATION (§8.4.3.3.3 SR2) and lower-case keywords both work. Residual, recorded but not verdict-changing: NEITHER cited test exercises the rule's own content — the arity bound (zero / two / non-keyword arguments) and the NESTED and STACK keywords are pinned by no test at all, so the structural enforcement I verified by hand is undefended against drift. Editions re-derived from the SPEC, not the catalog row: Annex E.3.3 item 28 (checked) plus Annex F.13 item 13, which lists MODULE-NAME among the intrinsic names ADDED by this edition. EVIDENCE: New probes, already-built cobol.exe, --std 2023, control MNREFCTL1 succeeded ('CTL-CUR=[MNREFCTL1]'). Keyword-omitted: E:/Temp/mnref/omit.cob (REPOSITORY. FUNCTION MODULE-NAME INTRINSIC) -> 'OMIT-CUR=[MNREFOMIT1]' / 'OMIT-TOP=[MNREFOMIT1]'; omitall.cob (FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) -> 'ALL-CUR=[MNREFALL1]'; omitnest.cob -> 'IN-NST=[MNROMNS1-IN]' 'IN-ACT=[MNROMNS1]' 'IN-STK=[MNROMNS1; ]' (the reserved word NESTED survives the ReparseArgs round trip). Ref-mod: refmod.cob 'FUNCTION MODULE-NAME(CURRENT) (1:3)' -> 'RM=[MNR]'. Case: lower.cob '(current)' -> 'LOW=[MNREFLOW1]' (KeywordWordOf upper-cases). Rejections re-run: emptyp.cob '()' -> COBOL1504 'requires one keyword argument'; figarg.cob '(SPACE)' and badarg.cob '(TE(1))' -> COBOL1504 "...not 'SPACE'" / "...not 'TE(1)'". Edition sweep EXTENDED past the adjudicator's single 2014 point: ctl.cob at --std 85 and --std 2002 both -> COBOL1502 'introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2023'. Citations checked: `cite.py --check E.3.3 "The MODULE-NAME intrinsic function has been added to provide information about the modules in the hierarchy of the running application."` -> OK item 28; §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 and §12.3.8 SR13 read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md; Annex F.13 item 13 lists MODULE-NAME.
